chunks: Ahmad, al-Hasan, and Abu Shu'ayb, from Abi Jamilah, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: concerning
Regarding a slave who kills a free man intentionally, he said: “One hundred mature camels; and if there are no camels, then in place of each camel, twenty head from the male sheep.”

As for dirhams, no more than ten thousand dirhams are binding, and most of the narrations have come with that. As for what was narrated by 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan and 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah, the two reports that contained twelve thousand dirhams, al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa both mentioned that our companions narrated that this was according to a weight of six; and if that is so, then it returns to ten thousand, and there is no contradiction between the reports.

key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمُ: dirhams; monetary equivalent discussed for diyah
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the reports; the narrations being reconciled
key_terms.الْإِبِلِ الْمَسَانِّ: mature camels; the primary form of diyah mentioned
key_terms.الْعَبْدِ: the slave; the legal subject discussed in the ruling
key_terms.حُرًّا: a free man; the victim whose status affects the diyah ruling
key_terms.عَشَرَةِ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ: ten thousand dirhams; the binding monetary amount
key_terms.فُحُولَةِ الْغَنَمِ: male sheep; substitute livestock valuation in the absence of camels

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for a slave who intentionally kills a free man according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the diyah for a slave who intentionally kills a free man, specifying compensation in camels or, if unavailable, in sheep. It also clarifies the amount in dirhams and reconciles apparently differing reports by explaining a difference in weight standard, thus removing contradiction between the narrations.
